critical_code_review_comments: auth.py L76: viewer.domains=['hospital','traffic'] intentional per iter-11 spec — but /app/memory/test_credentials.md still says 'Viewer | ALL DOMAINS (read-only)'. Update the memory doc so future testers don't assume viewer can read energy/water.

twins.py _guard_read L1061-1062: 'if user is None: return' — the fallback silently allows anonymous access if a caller wires the router without user_dep. Current wiring via _resolve_user_dep DOES enforce auth (unauth 401 confirmed), so risk is low, but consider hard-failing when user is None to prevent future regressions.

server.py L744 WS auth: reads token from cookie OR ?token= query. Query param tokens are logged by proxies (cloudflare access logs show query strings). Prefer cookie-only for production; keep query support gated to dev/preview.

server.py L676-679 AIRA refusal returns 200 with plain-text 'not authorised' body — semantically this should probably be HTTP 403. Client currently parses the string, which is brittle. Consider structured refusal (JSON with authorised=false).
test_credentials: super@twin.platform, hospital@twin.platform, energy@twin.platform, traffic@twin.platform, viewer@twin.platform — all password Twin@2026 (viewer scope: hospital+traffic only)
seed_data_creation: Test flips energy substation sub-2 to isolated via super admin action (cascades to transformers/feeders) and toggles water simulation running=true. No new users seeded.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run backend: python -m pytest /app/tests/test_iter11_rbac.py -o addopts='' -v. Action endpoint payload shape is {action, params:{}} (NOT {action, target}). WebSocket URL: wss://{host}/api/ws/twins?token={jwt} — token via query works in preview, cookie is preferred. Unauthenticated WS is rejected via HTTP 403 at the accept handshake (websockets lib surfaces InvalidStatus). AIRA refusal comes back as HTTP 200 with body containing 'not authorised' — assertion should be substring, not status_code. Sidebar locked stubs (nav-d-{d}-locked) only render on platform-home key='platform' rail — NOT on domain-scoped pages like /hospital/wards which show nav-h-* instead. Chips are always visible from any page.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found this iteration. RBAC matrix (9 roles × 6 domains × read/write) is correctly enforced at every layer: HTTP guards in twins.py + server.py, WebSocket auth + per-envelope filtering in /api/ws/twins, AIRA domain gate in assistant_stream, plus UI locks (tiles, sidebar stubs, chips, action buttons, notif filter, page-access-denied route wrapper).
